## 14. Publication-quality supplemental figures

Figure S1 is assembled in the final chunk (`fig-s1-combined`) from five
panel inputs across three rows:

- **Panel A (Row 1, full width):** `p_C_storm` — CTD + NOAA pressure traces; built in `build-storm-traces` below
- **Panel B (Row 2, full width):** `p_D_detided` — storm-driven water level anomaly; built in `build-detided-anomaly` below
- **Panel C (Row 3, left):** `p_lag_major` — propagation lag boxplot; built in `build-lag-boxplot` above
- **Panel D (Row 3, middle):** `p_flux` — asymmetric flux boxplot; built upstream in Section 12.4 (`gap-asymmetric-flux`)
- **Panel E (Row 3, right):** `p_residence` — residence time boxplot; built in `build-residence-boxplot` above

Row 3 panels share a single fill aesthetic (tidal regime: Spring / Neap)
in a two-tone blue palette; patchwork collects them into one shared legend
placed at the right of the row via `guide_area()`. Panel widths within
Row 3 are 4 : 4 : 6 : 4 (lag : flux : residence : legend area) — each
x-axis category gets the same horizontal space across panels (2 width-units
per category: lag and flux have two categories each, residence has three).
This keeps the rendered box widths visually consistent across all three
panels.

Intermediate panel objects below carry no letter prefix; the assembly
chunk applies the final panel letters via `plot_annotation(tag_levels = ...)`.

```{r build-lag-boxplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, dpi=300}
# Builds p_lag_major — lag boxplot panel in Figure S1 row 3 (left).
# Boxplots of independent CTD/NOAA propagation lag, x-axis = tide type
# (High / Low), fill = tidal regime (Spring / Neap). Two-tone blue palette
# unifies the regime aesthetic with the flux and residence boxplots.
#
# Filter to Spring/Neap BEFORE factoring: lag_data carries Intermediate
# regime rows too; without the filter, factor() coerces them to NA and
# ggplot renders an extra grey "NA" boxplot group with NA in the legend.
# The flux and residence panels filter identically (Sections 12.4 and
# build-residence-boxplot respectively) — this matches that pattern.
lag_plot_major <- lag_data %>%
  filter(tidal_regime %in% c("Spring", "Neap")) %>%
  mutate(tide_label   = factor(if_else(noaa_type == "H", "High", "Low"),
                               levels = c("High", "Low")),
         tidal_regime = factor(tidal_regime,
                               levels = c("Spring", "Neap")))

p_lag_major <- ggplot(lag_plot_major,
                      aes(x = tide_label, y = ind_lag_min, fill = tidal_regime)) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = "errorbar", width = 0.3,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, outlier.size = 1.2,
               outlier.color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Spring" = "#3288BD",   # Spectral blue (stronger forcing)
                               "Neap"   = "#9ECAE1"),  # Lightened (weaker forcing)
                    name = "Tidal regime") +
  labs(x = "Tide type", y = "Tidal propagation lag\n(minutes)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.margin = margin(t = 6, r = 6, b = 4, l = 6))

print(p_lag_major)
```

```{r build-residence-boxplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, dpi=300}
# Builds p_residence — Figure S1 Panel F (fig-s1-combined assembly).
# Boxplots of geometric tidal residence time per half-cycle, x-axis = storm
# phase (Pre-storm / Storm / Post-storm), fill = tidal regime (Spring /
# Neap). Uses position_dodge2(preserve = "single") so box widths remain
# consistent across the empty Spring × Storm cell (the storm coincided
# with the Neap regime, so no Spring data exist in the storm window).
residence_plot_data <- half_cycle %>%
  filter(period %in% c("Pre-storm", "Storm", "Post-storm"),
         tidal_regime %in% c("Spring", "Neap"),
         !is.na(residence_d), residence_d > 0) %>%
  mutate(period       = factor(period,
                               levels = c("Pre-storm", "Storm", "Post-storm")),
         tidal_regime = factor(tidal_regime,
                               levels = c("Spring", "Neap")))

p_residence <- ggplot(residence_plot_data,
                      aes(x = period, y = residence_d, fill = tidal_regime)) +
  stat_boxplot(geom = "errorbar", width = 0.6,
               position = position_dodge2(width = 0.7, preserve = "single"),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6,
               position = position_dodge2(width = 0.7, preserve = "single"),
               color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, outlier.size = 1.2,
               outlier.color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Spring" = "#3288BD",   # Spectral blue (stronger forcing)
                               "Neap"   = "#9ECAE1"),  # Lightened (weaker forcing)
                    name = "Tidal regime") +
  labs(x = "Storm phase", y = "Tidal residence time\n(days)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.margin = margin(t = 6, r = 6, b = 4, l = 6))

print(p_residence)
```

```{r build-storm-traces, fig.width=10, fig.height=4, dpi=300}
# Builds p_C_storm — used as Panel A in Figure S1 (fig-s1-combined).
# Continuous CTD + NOAA pressure traces over an expanded Fig S1 window
# (Jul 11 – Aug 11) capturing both full moons flanking the analytical
# pre/post-storm windows. Date range matches detided panel below for
# stacked-panel alignment. Wider window affects only the plot; analytical
# periods (pre-storm, storm, post-storm) remain anchored to STORM_START ±
# PRE_STORM_DAYS / POST_STORM_DAYS as defined upstream.

# ── Plotting window: bounded exactly by the two full moons ──
# Edges coincide with the Jul 12 and Aug 10 full moons (16:25 and 08:09 HST
# respectively). Tiny x-axis expansion (0.5%) keeps moon dashed lines just
# inside the panel edges, visible against the y-axis line. Slightly wider
# than the analytical calculation window (Jul 13 – Aug 6) on the right
# (~4 days), capturing additional recovery context without affecting any
# pre/storm/post period assignments upstream.
fig_s1_start <- as_datetime("2014-07-11 16:25:00", tz = "Pacific/Honolulu")  # 1 day before first full moon — creates space for moon icon next to "Full" label
fig_s1_end   <- as_datetime("2014-08-10 08:09:00", tz = "Pacific/Honolulu")

ctd_plot_window <- ctd %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end)

noaa_plot_window <- noaa_obs %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end) %>%
  # Convert NOAA water level (m above MLLW datum) to dbar for direct overlay
  # with CTD pressure. Factor 1.006 = ρ × g / 10⁴ for seawater at ~25 °C, 35 PSU
  # (ρ ≈ 1025 kg/m³, g = 9.81 m/s², 10⁴ converts Pa to dbar). The same factor is
  # reversed (÷ 1.006) on the panel"s secondary y-axis to display equivalent m.
  mutate(verified_dbar = verified_m * 1.006)

# ── Moon phase markers within plotting window (HST) ──
moon_phases <- tribble(
  ~date,                   ~label,
  "2014-07-12 16:25:00",   "Full",
  "2014-07-18 16:08:00",   "Last Q",
  "2014-07-26 12:42:00",   "New",
  "2014-08-03 14:50:00",   "First Q",
  "2014-08-10 08:09:00",   "Full"
) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as_datetime(date, tz = "Pacific/Honolulu")) %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end)

# Diagnostic: confirm parsing succeeded
message("Moon phases parsed (should be 5 rows, no NA datetimes):")
print(moon_phases)

# ── Sampling event datetimes (10 discrete sampling dates) ──
# YSI/discrete water samples from Methods. Used for tick marks above plot.
sampling_dates <- tribble(
  ~date_str,
  "2014-07-07", "2014-07-09", "2014-07-14", "2014-07-16",
  "2014-07-21", "2014-07-23", "2014-07-24", "2014-07-29",
  "2014-07-30", "2014-08-06"
) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as_datetime(paste(date_str, "12:00:00"),
                                tz = "Pacific/Honolulu")) %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end)

p_C_storm <- ggplot() +
  # Storm shading (extends back to rainfall onset on Oahu, ~18:00 HST Jul 19)
  annotate("rect", xmin = as_datetime(STORM_SHADING_START), xmax = as_datetime(STORM_SHADING_END),
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#dfdfdf", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Moon phase vertical dashed lines (darker grey, thicker for visibility)
  geom_vline(data = moon_phases, aes(xintercept = datetime),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Moon phase labels in top margin (requires clip = "off" below)
  geom_text(data = moon_phases,
            aes(x = datetime, y = Inf, label = label),
            vjust = -2.8, size = 5, color = "grey30", hjust = 0.5) +
  # CTD and NOAA traces — NOAA drawn first (behind), CTD on top.
  # Both lines solid; color and thickness distinguish them. HFP (CTD)
  # is thicker solid black as the primary fishpond signal; NOAA bay
  # reference is thinner solid Spectral purple behind.
  geom_line(data = noaa_plot_window,
            aes(x = datetime, y = verified_dbar, color = "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)"),
            linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = ctd_plot_window,
            aes(x = datetime, y = pressure, color = "CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)"),
            linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Sampling event markers (small downward triangles at panel top edge)
  geom_point(data = sampling_dates,
             aes(x = datetime, y = Inf),
             shape = 25, fill = "black", color = "black",
             size = 2, stroke = 0.35) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL,
                     values = c("CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)" = "black",
                                "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)"    = "#5E4FA2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1.006, name = "Water level\n(m)")
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%b %d", date_breaks = "3 days",
                   date_minor_breaks = "1 day",
                   limits = c(fig_s1_start, fig_s1_end),
                   expand = expansion(mult = 0.005)) +
  guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +   # allow moon labels + triangles to render in top margin
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Water level\n(dbar)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),  # x-labels suppressed; detided panel below carries them
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        # Right axis (NOAA conversion to meters) styled in Spectral purple
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.text.y.right  = element_text(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.line.y.right  = element_line(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 38, r = 6, b = 4, l = 6))  # extra top margin for moon labels + triangles

print(p_C_storm)
```

```{r build-detided-anomaly, fig.width=10, fig.height=4, dpi=300}
# Builds p_D_detided — used as Panel B in Figure S1 (fig-s1-combined).
# Plots two detided water level signals as anomalies from each signal"s
# pre-storm mean: CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond, sediment-water interface) and
# NOAA (Moku o Loʻe, MLLW reference). Each signal detided via a 25-h
# centered running mean, then centered on its own pre-storm mean
# (datetime < STORM_START within the analytical pre-storm window).
#
# Anomaly framing necessary because the two signals reference different
# absolute baselines; subtracting pre-storm means puts them on a common
# y-axis where storm impact is directly comparable. The contrast between
# CTD and NOAA storm-period anomalies isolates the freshwater-driven
# component of fishpond water level elevation from any bay-side storm
# surge component.
#
# Uses the same expanded plotting window as Panel A (fig_s1_start/end,
# defined in build-storm-traces) so the two panels stack with aligned
# date axes.

# ── CTD detided (25-h running mean) ──
ctd_interval <- as.numeric(median(diff(ctd$datetime), units = "mins"))
ctd_window_n <- round(25 * 60 / ctd_interval)

ctd_detided <- ctd %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  mutate(mean_wl = zoo::rollmean(pressure, k = ctd_window_n,
                                 fill = NA, align = "center"))

# ── NOAA detided (same 25-h running mean, converted to dbar) ──
noaa_interval <- as.numeric(median(diff(noaa_obs$datetime), units = "mins"))
noaa_window_n <- round(25 * 60 / noaa_interval)

noaa_detided <- noaa_obs %>%
  filter(datetime >= fig_s1_start, datetime <= fig_s1_end) %>%
  arrange(datetime) %>%
  mutate(verified_dbar = verified_m * 1.006,
         mean_wl = zoo::rollmean(verified_dbar, k = noaa_window_n,
                                 fill = NA, align = "center"))

# ── Compute anomalies (subtract each signal"s pre-storm mean) ──
ctd_pre_mean <- ctd_detided %>%
  filter(datetime < STORM_START, datetime >= pre_storm_start) %>%
  summarise(ref = mean(mean_wl, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(ref)

noaa_pre_mean <- noaa_detided %>%
  filter(datetime < STORM_START, datetime >= pre_storm_start) %>%
  summarise(ref = mean(mean_wl, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(ref)

ctd_anomaly <- ctd_detided %>%
  mutate(anomaly = mean_wl - ctd_pre_mean, source = "CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)")
noaa_anomaly <- noaa_detided %>%
  mutate(anomaly = mean_wl - noaa_pre_mean, source = "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)")

detided_combined <- bind_rows(
  ctd_anomaly  %>% select(datetime, anomaly, source),
  noaa_anomaly %>% select(datetime, anomaly, source)
) %>%
  mutate(source = factor(source,
                         levels = c("CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)",
                                    "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)")))

message(sprintf("Pre-storm reference means — CTD: %.4f dbar, NOAA: %.4f dbar",
                ctd_pre_mean, noaa_pre_mean))
message(sprintf("Storm-period max anomaly — CTD: %.4f, NOAA: %.4f",
                max(ctd_anomaly$anomaly[ctd_anomaly$datetime >= STORM_START &
                                         ctd_anomaly$datetime <= STORM_END],
                    na.rm = TRUE),
                max(noaa_anomaly$anomaly[noaa_anomaly$datetime >= STORM_START &
                                          noaa_anomaly$datetime <= STORM_END],
                    na.rm = TRUE)))

p_D_detided <- ggplot(detided_combined,
                      aes(x = datetime, y = anomaly)) +
  # Storm shading (extends back to rainfall onset on Oahu, ~18:00 HST Jul 19)
  annotate("rect", xmin = as_datetime(STORM_SHADING_START), xmax = as_datetime(STORM_SHADING_END),
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#dfdfdf", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Moon phase vertical dashed lines (lines only; labels are on Panel A above)
  geom_vline(data = moon_phases, aes(xintercept = datetime),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Two geom_lines for source-specific linewidth — both solid, but
  # NOAA bay reference rendered thinner and behind CTD (drawn first),
  # then CTD fishpond signal rendered thicker on top.
  geom_line(data = filter(detided_combined, source == "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)"),
            aes(color = source), linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = filter(detided_combined, source == "CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)"),
            aes(color = source), linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL,
                     values = c("CTD (Heʻeia Fishpond)" = "black",
                                "NOAA (Moku o Loʻe)"    = "#5E4FA2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 1.006, name = "Water level anomaly\n(m, 25-hr mean)")
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%b %d", date_breaks = "3 days",
                   date_minor_breaks = "1 day",
                   limits = c(fig_s1_start, fig_s1_end),
                   expand = expansion(mult = 0.005)) +
  guides(x = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Water level anomaly\n(dbar, 25-hr mean)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        # Right axis (NOAA conversion to meters) styled in Spectral purple
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.text.y.right  = element_text(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.line.y.right  = element_line(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "#5E4FA2"),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 4, r = 6, b = 4, l = 6))

print(p_D_detided)
```

```{r fig-s1-combined, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, dpi=300}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Figure S1: Combined tidal dynamics figure (5 panels, 3 rows)
#
#   Row 1: Panel A — CTD + NOAA pressure traces       (full width)
#   Row 2: Panel B — Storm-driven water level anomaly (full width)
#   Row 3: Panel C lag | Panel D flux | Panel E residence | legend area
#          Widths 4 : 4 : 6 : 4 (2 width-units per x-axis category;
#          legend gets ~22% of the row)
#
# Row 3 panels share a single fill aesthetic (Tidal regime: Spring / Neap)
# rendered in a two-tone blue palette, so patchwork collects one shared
# legend placed in the rightmost guide_area().
#
# Panel A"s bottom axis line, ticks, and labels are suppressed so it flows
# visually into Panel B below as a continuous time series. Panel B carries
# x-axis ticks/date labels for both rows. Panel A"s CTD/NOAA legend is also
# suppressed; Panel B"s legend carries the source key for both rows.
#
# Panels A and B share x-axis range (fig_s1_start through fig_s1_end,
# defined in build-storm-traces: full-moon-to-full-moon Jul 11 16:25 –
# Aug 10 08:09 HST) so storm box, moon-phase lines, and date ticks
# align across both rows.
#
# Tag list explicitly skips the guide_area so panel letters remain A–E
# (assigned in plotting order: p_A_final → A, p_D_detided → B, then
# row3"s lag/flux/residence → C/D/E; the trailing "" suppresses any
# tag on the legend guide_area).
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Panel A: hide bottom axis line + ticks, remove legend ──
# Panel B below carries the x-axis date labels AND the CTD/NOAA
# source legend for both panels.
p_A_final <- p_C_storm +
  theme(axis.line.x.bottom = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x       = element_blank(),
        legend.position    = "none")

# ── Row 3 panel preparation ──
# Remove individual legends from the lag, flux, and residence panels so
# patchwork"s guide_area() collects a single shared "Tidal regime" legend
# for the whole row.
p_lag_panel       <- p_lag_major + theme(legend.position = "none")
p_flux_panel      <- p_flux      + theme(legend.position = "none")
p_residence_panel <- p_residence + theme(legend.position = "none")

# Row 3 layout: Panels C / D / E + shared legend in guide_area().
# Widths chosen so each x-axis category gets the same horizontal space
# across panels (2 width-units per category): lag and flux have 2
# categories each → width 4; residence has 3 categories → width 6.
# This keeps the rendered box width visually consistent across all three
# panels. The legend area gets 4 (~22% of the row). Total = 18 units.
row3 <- p_lag_panel + p_flux_panel + p_residence_panel + guide_area() +
  plot_layout(widths = c(4, 4, 6, 4), guides = "collect")

# Full figure assembly with explicit panel letters. The tag_levels list
# has six entries to match the six elements patchwork sees (A, B, then
# row3"s four elements: three panels + the guide_area, which gets "" so
# no letter prints on the legend region).
fig_s1 <- p_A_final / p_D_detided / row3 +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = list(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", ""))) &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22, hjust = 0, vjust = 1),
        plot.tag.position = c(0.01, 0.98),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(fig_s1)

ggsave(file.path(figure_path, "tidal_dynamics.pdf"),
       fig_s1, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = 300, device = "pdf")
```

## 15. Draft supplementary text (Methods / Results / Discussion)

```{r draft-text, results="asis"}
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Live-value handles for use in the draft text below.
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

lag_maj <- lag_overall

# Lag values by regime (for one-line summaries)
lag_high_spring <- lag_by_regime %>%
  filter(tide_type == "H", tidal_regime == "Spring")
lag_high_neap   <- lag_by_regime %>%
  filter(tide_type == "H", tidal_regime == "Neap")

# Residence time means by regime (regime-only summary; computed in 12.2)
res_spring  <- res_summary$mean_res_d[res_summary$tidal_regime == "Spring"]
res_neap    <- res_summary$mean_res_d[res_summary$tidal_regime == "Neap"]

# Storm-extended residence (neap, as illustrative example)
res_neap_pre   <- res_by_period$mean_res_d[res_by_period$period == "Pre-storm"   & res_by_period$tidal_regime == "Neap"]
res_neap_storm <- res_by_period$mean_res_d[res_by_period$period == "Storm"       & res_by_period$tidal_regime == "Neap"]

# Storm water level elevation (continuous 25-h mean)
storm_mean_wl <- mean_wl_by_period$mean_pressure_dbar[mean_wl_by_period$period == "Storm"]
pre_mean_wl   <- mean_wl_by_period$mean_pressure_dbar[mean_wl_by_period$period == "Pre-storm"]
storm_elev    <- storm_mean_wl - pre_mean_wl  # ~0.014 dbar
```

```{r print-supp-methods, results="asis"}
cat("\n\n### Supplementary Methods — Tidal dynamics analysis\n\n")

cat("To characterize how the restricted mākāhā connections modulate tidal exchange between Heʻeia Fishpond and Kāneʻohe Bay, we compared in-situ CTD pressure inside the fishpond with NOAA verified water levels at Station MOKH1 (Moku o Loʻe Island; NOAA CO-OPS, 2014) over the 67-day study period (10 June – 15 August 2014). Heʻeia Fishpond connects to Kāneʻohe Bay through three ocean mākāhā: Nui (OM1), Hīhīmanu (OM2), and Kahoalahui (Triple Mākāhā, TM), and to the upstream watershed through two river mākāhā: Waimāʻama (RM2) and Kaneloa (RM3) (Tognacchini, 2015). Two historical mākāhā remained unrestored at the time of this study: Wai (RM1), where wall breakage left a diffuse flow region between the wetland and the fishpond's northeast corner, and Kahoʻokele (Ocean Break), where a 50-m temporary wall of reduced height stood in place of the degraded original, permitting shallow surface-water exchange via overflow at higher tides.\n\n")

cat("Kāneʻohe Bay exhibits a mixed semi-diurnal tide in which each tidal day comprises two unequal high–low cycles: a major (larger amplitude) constituent and a minor (smaller amplitude) constituent. The mākāhā filter the minor constituent almost entirely, such that fishpond water level resolves only the major cycle (~12 h period) rather than the bay's two-cycle-per-day signal. We therefore restricted lag and flux analyses to major-constituent extrema, classified using NOAA harmonic predictions and confirmed against an independent peak-detection algorithm applied to the CTD signal. We further classified each cycle by lunar regime — spring, intermediate, or neap — based on proximity to syzygy or quadrature.\n\n")

cat("Tidal propagation lag was computed as the time difference between paired NOAA and CTD extrema of the same type (high or low) within a ±3 h matching window. Tidal flux was computed as the rate of pressure change between consecutive CTD extrema, with flooding and ebbing cycles separated by direction. Flood-versus-ebb rate comparisons within each lunar regime used a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test.\n\n")

cat(sprintf(
"We estimated tidal residence time using a tidal-prism approximation: τ = (V̄ / P_half) × T_half, where V̄ is mean fishpond volume, P_half is the half-cycle tidal prism (excursion × surface area), and T_half is the half-cycle period. We estimated V̄ as ~%.0f m³ from a fishpond surface area of %.0f m² and a mean tidal-cycle water column depth of %.2f m. We derived this mean depth from the bathymetric measurements of Tognacchini (2015), who reports a mean fishpond water column depth of %.2f m at neap low water and an average tidal range of %.2f m, as the neap low-water depth plus half the average tidal range (%.2f m + %.2f m).\n\n",
  mean_volume_m3, FISHPOND_AREA_M2, mean_depth_m,
  NEAP_LW_DEPTH_M, AVG_TIDAL_RANGE_M,
  NEAP_LW_DEPTH_M, AVG_TIDAL_RANGE_M / 2
))
```

```{r print-supp-results, results="asis"}
cat("\n\n### Supplementary Results — Storm Wali extended an already restricted and asymmetric tidal exchange\n\n")

cat(sprintf(
"Tidal extrema at Heʻeia Fishpond consistently lagged those at Moku o Loʻe. High tides at the fishpond lagged the open-ocean peak by a median of %.0f min (mean %.0f ± %.0f min, n = %d cycles), while low tides lagged by a median of %.0f min (mean %.0f ± %.0f min, n = %d cycles). Lag varied with tidal regime: high tides lagged by %.0f ± %.0f min during spring tides and %.0f ± %.0f min during neap tides, with intermediate cycles falling between (Table S3, Panel A). Low-tide lags exceeded high-tide lags across all regimes.\n\n",
  lag_maj$median_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "H"],
  lag_maj$mean_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "H"],
  lag_maj$sd_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "H"],
  lag_maj$n[lag_maj$tide_type == "H"],
  lag_maj$median_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "L"],
  lag_maj$mean_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "L"],
  lag_maj$sd_lag[lag_maj$tide_type == "L"],
  lag_maj$n[lag_maj$tide_type == "L"],
  lag_high_spring$mean_lag, lag_high_spring$sd_lag,
  lag_high_neap$mean_lag,   lag_high_neap$sd_lag
))

# Pull flood/ebb test rows for sprintf
fe_spring <- flood_ebb_test %>% filter(tidal_regime == "Spring")
fe_neap   <- flood_ebb_test %>% filter(tidal_regime == "Neap")

cat(sprintf(
"Mean pressure change rate during rising tides exceeded that during falling tides at spring tides (%.3f vs. %.3f dbar h⁻¹; Wilcoxon p = %s; Figure S1, Panel E; Table S3, Panel B). At neap tides, when astronomical forcing was weakest, the asymmetry collapsed (flood:ebb ratio = %.2f, p = %.2f); flow rates dropped near-equally in both directions. Half-cycle counts differed slightly between rising and falling within each regime due to major/minor cycle filtering and excursion thresholds (Table S3, Panel B); reported asymmetry ratios are robust to this imbalance.\n\n",
  fe_spring$rising_mean, fe_spring$falling_mean, formatC(fe_spring$p_value, format = "e", digits = 1),
  fe_neap$asymmetry_ratio, fe_neap$p_value
))

cat(sprintf(
"Tropical Storm Wali (20–23 July 2014) elevated mean fishpond water level. The continuous 25-h mean rose ~%.3f dbar above the pre-storm baseline during the storm and remained slightly elevated for ~5–6 days post-storm (Figure S1, Panel B), consistent with combined storm surge and freshwater runoff temporarily raising the fishpond baseline. The storm window coincided with the transition from neap to spring tides, with last quarter occurring on ~18–21 July (Table S3, Panel C).\n\n",
  storm_elev
))

cat(sprintf(
"Geometric tidal residence time varied with lunar regime: ~%.1f d at spring tides and ~%.1f d at neap tides. Storm Wali extended neap-regime residence time substantially (neap τ rose from ~%.1f d pre-storm to ~%.1f d during the storm, a ~%.0f%%%% increase). These geometric estimates align with the empirical tidal-exchange measurements of Tognacchini (2015), who measured 73%%%% volumetric water exchange per spring tidal cycle and 33%%%% per neap tidal cycle at the northeast study site, corresponding to residence-time scales of ~0.7 d at spring and ~1.6 d at neap.\n\n",
  res_spring, res_neap,
  res_neap_pre, res_neap_storm,
  100 * (res_neap_storm / res_neap_pre - 1)
))
```

```{r print-supp-discussion, results="asis"}
cat("\n\n### Supplementary Discussion — Mākāhā hydraulics link storm forcing to extended residence time and delayed microbial recovery\n\n")

cat("The lag and flux results together describe the mechanical character of tidal exchange through the mākāhā. Low-tide lags exceeding high-tide lags across all regimes (Supplementary Results, Table S3 Panel A) indicate that hydraulic restriction is greater on outflow (ebbing) than on inflow (flooding). The flood-versus-ebb rate asymmetry observed at spring and intermediate regimes (2.4–2.8×) supports the same mechanism from a different angle: hydraulic head drives faster flood through the mākāhā than gravity-only drainage on the ebb, and the asymmetry collapses at neap tides when the head differential itself becomes negligible. These two independent observations — lag asymmetry and rate asymmetry — point to the same physical bottleneck: the mākāhā impose a unidirectionally restricted exchange whose magnitude scales with astronomical forcing.\n\n")

cat(sprintf(
"The storm-period water level elevation observed in the detided continuous record (~%.3f dbar above the pre-storm baseline for ~5–6 days; Figure S1 Panel B) provides the cleanest visual evidence of Storm Wali's impact on fishpond hydrology. We cannot cleanly separate storm forcing from the natural neap reduction in tidal forcing in the major-cycle extrema data, because the storm window coincided with the neap-to-spring transition; the detided continuous record is free of this regime confound and isolates the storm-driven baseline shift.\n\n",
  storm_elev
))

cat("Storm-extended residence time provides a hydrological mechanism for the protracted microbial-community recovery documented in the main text. Our geometric residence-time estimate (~30–50% extension during the storm window relative to pre-storm baseline within each regime) is consistent with the prolonged freshwater plume persistence (~19 days) that Tognacchini (2015) documented at Heʻeia Fishpond following Wali, well beyond the average HFP recovery scale of ~4 days reported by Timmermann et al. (in prep.). The convergence of three independent measurements — our geometric tidal-prism estimate, Tognacchini's volumetric exchange ratios, and the plume persistence finding — supports the inference that reduced tidal exchange under combined storm and neap forcing extended water-mass residence in the fishpond during the disturbance window, providing prolonged contact time between fishpond water and the perturbed microbial-community state before bay-water exchange could reassert.\n\n")
```
